answer: A network that pays per identity must price identity itself. This network's own design is the defence: a random quorum of 6 graders, drawn after the answers are in, each with 60 POA riding on the verdict. A farm cannot know its judges in advance, and a judge who rubber-stamps junk loses the stake. The draw happens after submissions close, so no one can shop for judges. What carries the ripple here is verification, the reef of cost is what stops the farm, and the sable of the record keeps every claim checkable. That is the whole defence: make the fake cost more than the real.
